themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 5 this week vs. a 1.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 264% increase (z-score: 5.21)—suggesting rapid, recent growth in unlicensed or problematic cannabis retail operations in Bed-Stuy that may warrant enforcement investigation.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
First recent signal of this type in district complaint data
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed dispensaries operating openly in Bed-Stuy despite state licensing restrictions?
What enforcement actions has the city taken on problem retailers this week, and are NYPD/DOH tracking this spike?

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints reached 6 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 4,700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—indicating a sudden emergence of overgrown, debris-filled, or hazardous vacant lots that may threaten public health and safety across the district.
evidence: 6 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 17.76, highest severity in spike list)
4,700% increase—the single largest statistical anomaly in district data
No prior pattern; this is an emerging, localized crisis
reporting_angles: Map the 6 affected lots: are they concentrated in one neighborhood, or district-wide?
What triggered the spike—new demolitions, foreclosures, or deferred city maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints jumped to 18 last week vs. 3.2 weekly average—a 454% spike (z-score: 9.45)—suggesting a sudden rise in quality-of-life or low-level crime issues that residents are escalating to NYPD.
evidence: 18 non-emergency complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly average (z-score: 9.45)
454% increase marks second-highest spike by percentage
Suggests acute uptick in incidents residents deem police-worthy
reporting_angles: What specific non-emergency issues are driving the spike—trespassing, loitering, harassment, theft?
Are residents losing faith in 311 and calling police instead, or is there a genuine increase in street-level crime?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles & Graffiti Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, abandoned vehicle complaints climbed to 31 last week (182% above 11.0 weekly average, z-score: 4.78) and graffiti complaints hit 20 (191% above 6.9 average, z-score: 4.29)—a tandem rise suggesting deteriorating public infrastructure and possible gang activity or organized vandalism.
evidence: Abandoned vehicles: 31 complaints last week vs. 11.0 weekly average (182% increase, z-score: 4.78)
Graffiti: 20 complaints last week vs. 6.9 weekly average (191% increase, z-score: 4.29)
Two simultaneous spikes suggest coordinated neglect or vandalism, not random drift
reporting_angles: Are abandoned vehicles concentrated on specific blocks, suggesting chop-shop activity or dumping?
Is the graffiti tagged by known crews, or is it random vandalism—potential indicator of gang territory marking?

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage & Missing Signs
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 3 weeks, street sign complaints—both missing (3 complaints vs. 0.2 average, 1,100% increase) and damaged (3 complaints vs. 0.6 average, 380% increase)—suggest systematic neglect of wayfinding and traffic control infrastructure that may compound pedestrian and vehicle safety risks.
evidence: Missing street signs: 3 complaints (~3 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Damaged street signs: 3 complaints (last week) vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Combined signal: ~6 street sign complaints in 2-3 weeks vs. near-zero baseline
reporting_angles: What intersections or blocks have lost street signage—is this DOT maintenance backlog or targeted theft?
Has the city prioritized sign replacement in Bed-Stuy compared to other Brooklyn districts?
